docs.D01_business_overview.md:
Title: Music intellectual property and a global monetization platform
Source: compiled from: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20210303005864/en/Vivendi-The-Good-Results-for-2020-Confirm-the-Resilience-of-the-Groups-Main-Businesses; https://www.vivendi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/20210518_VIV_PR_Update-on-the-proposed-distribution-of-UMG-shares.pdf; https://www.ifpi.org/ifpi-issues-annual-global-music-report-2021
Date: 2021-05-18

Universal Music Group is a leading global recorded-music and music-publishing business within Vivendi. Its economics derive from developing artists, owning/licensing recordings and compositions, and monetizing consumption across physical, digital, performance and other channels.

Recorded music and publishing are related but distinct rights. Streaming services distribute music to users; labels and publishers license rights and compensate creators under their contracts. UMG is not the same business as a streaming application, and subscriber fees are not all label revenue.

Existing catalogs can be licensed repeatedly without manufacturing a new physical product for every listen. That provides attractive incremental economics. It does not eliminate artist royalties, advances, marketing, acquisition costs or the need to develop new repertoire.

The 2020 results show resilience during a difficult year. Recorded-music subscription/streaming revenue grew 16.2% at constant currency/perimeter, while merchandising suffered from limited touring. The exposure is therefore broader than a single recurring subscription line.

Lucian Grainge leads UMG. The recorded-music platform includes prominent artists and a deep catalog, while publishing extends exposure to composition rights. Competitive advantage depends on talent relationships, marketing/distribution scale, rights administration and a repertoire valuable to consumers and platforms.

Industry growth is supported by paid streaming. IFPI reports 443 million users of paid subscription accounts at the end of 2020, with subscription streaming revenue up 18.5%. Penetration and improved monetization can expand the industry, though lower-price markets and foreign exchange affect realized revenue per user.

UMG remains unlisted at this cutoff. Vivendi proposes distributing 60% of the equity and listing the company in Amsterdam by September 27 at the latest, subject to the process described in its May announcement.

The proposed governance includes one share/one vote, no poison pill and a largely non-executive board with a majority independent. These are proposals, not proof of an already independent completed public company.

The ownership opportunity combines a valuable rights franchise with a structural separation. The business merits analysis independently of transaction excitement: the investor needs a defensible price, normalized cash economics and confidence that artists, platforms and shareholders can all participate sustainably in industry growth.
docs.D02_financial_snapshot.md:
Title: UMG financial history within Vivendi, not a later prospectus reconstruction
Source: compiled from: https://www.vivendi.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/20200213_VIV_PR_2019_Vivendi_earnings.pdf; https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20210303005864/en/Vivendi-The-Good-Results-for-2020-Confirm-the-Resilience-of-the-Groups-Main-Businesses; https://www.vivendi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/20210518_VIV_PR_Update-on-the-proposed-distribution-of-UMG-shares.pdf
Date: 2021-05-18

Figures are millions of euros. These are UMG business disclosures from Vivendi releases available before June 3, not Vivendi consolidated totals and not September prospectus data.

| UMG metric | 2018 | 2019 | 2020 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 6,023 | 7,159 | 7,432 |
| EBITA | 902 | 1,124 | 1,329 |
| EBITA margin, calculated | 15.0% | 15.7% | 17.9% |

Actual revenue growth was 18.9% in 2019 and 3.8% in 2020. Constant-currency/perimeter growth was 14.0% and 4.7% respectively. EBITA grew 24.6% and 18.3% on an actual basis, with mix and cost control contributing.

EBITA is not EBITDA: amortization treatment differs, and neither equals net earnings or free cash flow. Applying an EBITDA multiple to this table without an explicit reconciliation would be incorrect.

The May 18 update supplies Q1 2021 standalone summary figures: revenue €1,809 million versus €1,769 million, EBIT €322 million versus €248 million, pretax earnings €164 million versus €144 million, and shareholder-attributable earnings €135 million versus €89 million.

Q1 EBIT margin calculated on reported revenue is 17.8%, up from 14.0%. Actual revenue growth is only 2.2%, versus 9.4% at constant currency/perimeter. Exchange rates materially affect the translation.

Net cash from operating activities before income tax was an outflow of €69 million in Q1. The release attributes improvement to operating performance and lower content spend. The measure is explicitly before tax and cannot be labeled ordinary after-tax FCF.

A complete pre-cutoff standalone CFO, capex, net debt, share count, diluted EPS and consolidated ROIC series was not independently recovered. The pack does not import the later listing prospectus to fill those fields.

The available evidence supports growing operating earning power and margin expansion. It leaves an important underwriting requirement: determine sustainable artist/content investment, working capital, taxes, standalone costs and separation debt before turning EBITA into equity cash yield or assigning an exact per-share intrinsic value.
docs.D03_latest_results.md:
Title: First-quarter growth, repertoire and cash timing
Source: compiled from: https://www.vivendi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/20210422_VIV_PR_Vivendi-revenues-Q1-2021.pdf; https://www.vivendi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/20210518_VIV_PR_Update-on-the-proposed-distribution-of-UMG-shares.pdf
Date: 2021-05-18

Vivendi's April 22 revenue release and May 18 UMG update are the latest retrieved operating disclosures before the cutoff. They report Q1 UMG revenue of €1,809 million, up 9.4% at constant currency/perimeter and 2.2% in actual euros.

Recorded-music revenue grew 10.8% at constant currency/perimeter. Subscription/streaming revenue increased 19.6%, despite comparison with a prior-year digital royalty claim. The underlying recurring growth is therefore stronger than the consolidated reported-euro headline.

Physical sales grew 14.8%, supported by new releases and catalog. Downloads declined 16.0%. These format differences matter: the company is participating in a transition rather than growing every legacy revenue stream.

Best sellers named in the release include new King & Prince and Justin Bieber releases and continued sales from The Weeknd, Ariana Grande and Pop Smoke. A diversified repertoire helps reduce dependence on one release but does not eliminate hit risk or contractual renewal risk.

Publishing revenue increased 6.9% at constant currency/perimeter, with subscription/streaming growth contributing. Publishing rights and recorded masters have different contracts and economics; their growth should not be mechanically merged into one royalty rate.

Merchandising/other revenue fell 10.0%, reflecting continued touring disruption, partly offset by retail and direct-to-consumer activity. The pandemic has therefore not been uniformly favorable to all music monetization.

EBIT reached €322 million versus €248 million, up 35.8% at constant currency/perimeter. Vivendi attributes the improvement to revenue growth and cost control. Q1 shareholder-attributable earnings were €135 million.

Cash flow before income tax was negative €69 million, despite positive operating profit. Content spending and working-capital timing matter. “Capital-light” does not mean reported profit immediately becomes distributable cash every quarter.

The May update also proposes governance for the prospective public company and discusses a possible additional stake sale. It does not provide a completed negotiated transaction, a guaranteed public opening price or a reliable standalone EPS forecast.

The investor can observe attractive streaming growth and operating leverage, while still needing a conservative conversion from current EBIT to normalized cash earnings. No later half-year figures, listing-day valuation or successful transaction are used to settle that question.
docs.D04_private_valuation.md:
Title: Pre-listing valuation anchors and missing equity terms
Source: compiled from: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20210303005864/en/Vivendi-The-Good-Results-for-2020-Confirm-the-Resilience-of-the-Groups-Main-Businesses; https://www.vivendi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/20210518_VIV_PR_Update-on-the-proposed-distribution-of-UMG-shares.pdf
Date: 2021-05-18

UMG has no public share-price, daily trading volume or 52-week range at June 3. A later Amsterdam opening quote cannot serve as an entry price in this pre-listing simulation.

The March Vivendi results identify the Tencent-led consortium's 20% investment at a €30 billion enterprise-value reference. This is a documented private transaction anchor, not proof that a new buyer can transact at the same terms.

At €30 billion EV, the ratio to 2020 UMG revenue of €7.432 billion is 4.04x. The ratio to 2020 EBITA of €1.329 billion is 22.6x. Those are explicitly EV/revenue and EV/EBITA calculations, not P/E or EV/EBITDA.

The May announcement says Vivendi is considering selling another 10% to an American investor or offering 5%-10% publicly before distributing 60%. It does not disclose a binding counterparty price in the information used here.

A 10% enterprise-value slice is not automatically the equity consideration for a 10% stake. Net debt, intercompany balances, transaction costs and separation arrangements affect equity value. Exact terms require more than a headline valuation.

The financial history shows improving EBITA margin, from 15.0% in 2018 to 17.9% in 2020. An underwriting model can test further operating leverage, but must allow for artist economics, standalone costs, marketing and content investment rather than assume pure royalty drop-through.

The proposed separation may make the music franchise easier for investors to value independently. A governance/listing catalyst can narrow a conglomerate discount without altering the underlying business, but it can also introduce shareholder-distribution selling, tax complexity and execution risk.

A verified pre-cutoff forward P/E, standalone FCF yield, net-debt table, consensus EPS series and comparable-company forward multiples were not recovered. No such figures are inferred from a later prospectus.

The valuation task is consequently enterprise-level and conditional: determine whether sustainable cash growth and the rights platform justify the negotiated price once actual equity terms are available. The existing transaction anchor provides discipline, not a guaranteed fair value or an instruction to accept any premium for scarcity.
docs.D05_market_concerns.md:
Title: Streaming opportunity with platform, artist and separation risks
Source: compiled from: https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/activist-fund-bluebell-calls-vivendi-sweeten-universal-spin-off-2021-05-25; https://www.ifpi.org/ifpi-issues-annual-global-music-report-2021; https://www.vivendi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/20210518_VIV_PR_Update-on-the-proposed-distribution-of-UMG-shares.pdf
Date: 2021-05-25

Reuters' May 25 report says activist Bluebell wants Vivendi to supplement the planned Universal distribution with a cash dividend more advantageous to minority shareholders. This is a real pre-cutoff dispute about transaction economics, not evidence of an already failed separation.

The dispute highlights a distinction between UMG's franchise quality and the return actually delivered through a holding-company distribution. Taxes, controlling-holder incentives and the route of ownership can affect minority outcomes even if the music business performs well.

Vivendi's May governance proposal includes one share/one vote, no poison pill and a majority-independent non-executive board. Those are favorable proposed terms, but approval and implementation remain conditions rather than established public-company practice.

Streaming offers recurring monetization and global reach, yet labels negotiate with powerful distribution platforms. Platform bargaining, promotional access and the allocation of subscription revenue can influence the economics captured by rights owners.

Artists and songwriters also bargain for compensation and control. Valuable catalog rights and talent-development scale support the franchise, but future repertoire requires advances, marketing and relationships. A model assuming all industry growth accrues to existing label shareholders would be incomplete.

IFPI reports strong 2020 paid-subscription growth alongside declines in physical and performance rights. Growth therefore depends on mix and monetization, not simply total listening. Lower-priced markets can add users with less revenue per account.

The May release's negative Q1 operating cash flow before tax is a reminder that content spending and cash timing remain material. The platform may have attractive incremental economics while still requiring investment and working capital.

The favorable view is that must-have repertoire participates across many distributors and formats, with catalog longevity supporting repeated revenue. The adverse view is that platforms, artists or a costly acquisition cycle capture more of the growth than equity investors expect.

No later generative-AI dispute, streaming repricing program, board conflict or listing outcome is imported. The authentic June 3 decision concerns established rights economics, a streaming growth runway and a proposed structural transaction whose terms and minority implications still require diligence.
docs.D06_peer_industry.md:
Title: Industry growth and Warner's contemporaneous operating evidence
Source: compiled from: https://www.ifpi.org/ifpi-issues-annual-global-music-report-2021; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1319161/000131916121000017/q22021ex991.htm; https://www.vivendi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/20210518_VIV_PR_Update-on-the-proposed-distribution-of-UMG-shares.pdf
Date: 2021-05-18

IFPI's March 23 Global Music Report says global recorded-music revenue rose 7.4% in 2020 to $21.6 billion, the sixth consecutive year of growth. Paid subscription streaming revenue rose 18.5% and paid-account users reached 443 million.

The growth is not a uniform rise across every format. The industry release identifies weaker physical/performance-rights categories alongside streaming expansion. Labels need to manage both the transition and the economics of new monetization.

Warner Music's May 4 release for the quarter ended March 31 provides a relevant public-company comparison. Revenue grew 17%, or 13% at constant currency, while digital revenue grew 23%, or 20% constant currency.

Warner's adjusted OIBDA rose 21% to $255 million from $210 million. Reported OIBDA was $228 million versus $12 million; net income was $117 million versus a prior-year $74 million loss. The large reported-versus-adjusted differences caution against naive headline-profit comparisons.

UMG's corresponding calendar-quarter revenue grew 9.4% at constant currency/perimeter and EBIT rose 35.8% on that basis to €322 million. Subscription/streaming revenue grew 19.6%. Both companies' evidence supports ongoing digital growth, but their reported profit definitions differ.

OIBDA, EBIT, EBITA and EBITDA are not interchangeable. Currency, acquisitions, release timing, rights mix and adjustments also affect comparability. No claim that one company has a superior margin is made by dividing incompatible measures.

Sony's music business is another relevant rights participant, but a comparable timestamped standalone table and valuation were not recovered. Nor was a verified June 3 Warner forward multiple. The pack does not invent a two-to-four-peer relative-valuation screen.

Industry growth helps validate the addressable trend, while the investor still must determine UMG's capture of value. Market growth can coexist with artist-cost inflation, catalog-acquisition competition and platform bargaining.

The useful benchmark is a rights business participating in a growing, increasingly digital market, not a software subscription company with no content obligations. The sector's recovery from prior disruption supports a growth hypothesis, but expected returns still depend on the private entry terms and normalized cash conversion.
docs.D07_structure_context.md:
Title: Separation timeline and vehicle-specific capital
Source: compiled from: https://www.vivendi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/20210518_VIV_PR_Update-on-the-proposed-distribution-of-UMG-shares.pdf; https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2021/02/18084718/PSH-2021-Annual-Investor-Presentation.pdf
Date: 2021-06-03

Vivendi's May 18 announcement describes a planned distribution of 60% of UMG and an Amsterdam listing by September 27 at the latest. It also discusses retaining 10% for at least two years and possibly selling an additional stake before the distribution.

The Tencent-led group already owns 20% according to the earlier results announcement. The proposed additional 10% sale is distinct from that existing investment and from the planned in-kind distribution.

The prospective public-company governance would observe one share/one vote, no poison pill, two-year director terms and a majority-independent non-executive board. Neither Vivendi nor Bolloré intends board representation at that stage. These are proposed arrangements subject to the process/consents described, not a final operating history.

The manager's February 18 presentation reports February 16 core funds total AUM of $13.562 billion and equity AUM $11.462 billion, with $2.1 billion PSH debt included in the first figure. PSH alone is $12.027 billion total/$9.927 billion equity.

PSTH's trust and commitments are separate from those core-fund assets. SPAC capital is not interchangeable with PSH cash, and a proposal by one vehicle does not establish ownership by another or the eventual economic outcome for its shareholders.

Precise June vehicle cash, current NAV weights and binding transaction terms are not recovered from qualifying pre-cutoff disclosures. A large negotiated stake would require explicit analysis of funding, approvals, custody, listing distribution and potential co-investment.

June 3 press items later updated on June 4 cannot safely be treated as evidence that Friday's official confirmation was already public. The pack therefore excludes the manager's confirmed proposed terms and identity as buyer, rather than use a misleading initial publication date.

This leaves an independent decision setup: a valuable music-rights platform approaching separation, an existing private valuation anchor and possible new stake availability. The investor must assess the business and structure without assuming the transaction closes, the listing trades at a particular price or the same investor vehicle ultimately owns the shares.

drivers.driver: Leading global music-rights/catalog platform acts as a royalty on growing consumption.
Paid streaming penetration and improved monetization offer a long runway.
Repeat licensing, scale and operating leverage support capital-light cash growth.
Lucian Grainge and patient ownership align with long-duration compounding.
Negotiated pre-listing ownership and separation can unlock independent valuation.

answer_key.pack_quality_notes: Seven documents. Strictly excludes June4-confirmed terms even from articles initially dated June3 but updated Friday. Uses2018-20 UMG EBITA/revenue, May18Q1 EBIT/cash, Tencent€30bn anchor and industry/Warner data. Standalone EPS, netdebt, fullFCF and peer multiples unavailable beforecutoff.

valuation.eps_path: Mid-to-high single digit growth driven by streaming adoption
valuation.downside_case: Multiple contraction to 15-18x EBITA if growth stalls or platform power compresses margins

drivers.driver: UMG is a dominant global leader in music intellectual property with a vast catalog and strong market position [D01].
The secular tailwind of paid music streaming provides a durable runway for long-term growth [D01, D06].
The spin-off from Vivendi acts as a catalyst to resolve governance concerns and unlock standalone valuation [D01, D07].
We see an opportunity to acquire a high-quality compounder that the market misprices due to short-term hit-driven volatility [D01, D05].

kill_criteria: Streaming platform revenue share shifts significantly against label interests
Failure to transition to standalone governance as proposed in the spin-off
Sustained inability to convert EBITA to free cash flow due to excessive content/A&R investment requirements
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence of consistent, robust standalone free cash flow generation and the successful implementation of the independent governance structure post-listing.
final.memo:
The Company represents a premier global music intellectual property business, commanding a leadership position through a deep, durable catalog and significant scale in artist development [D01, D05]. It meets our standard for a high-quality compounder, underpinned by the secular growth of paid streaming which continues to drive industry-wide expansion [D01, D06].

The opportunity arises from the upcoming separation from Vivendi, a transaction the market has complicated with concerns regarding governance and short-term, hit-driven financial volatility [D01, D05, D07]. We believe the market fails to properly appreciate the recurring, royalty-like nature of the catalog, which provides a level of predictability that is currently obscured by its status as a Vivendi subsidiary [D01, D06].

Based on an implied enterprise value of €30 billion, the business trades at approximately 22.6x 2020 EBITA [D04]. While this valuation reflects its quality, we project mid-to-high single-digit earnings growth, aiming for an internal rate of return that could exceed 20% in our bull case [D01, D06].

The spin-off process serves as our primary catalyst, expected to resolve governance uncertainties and allow the market to re-rate the entity as a standalone asset [D01, D07]. We anticipate that the adoption of a one-share/one-vote structure and a majority-independent board will provide the necessary alignment for long-term shareholder value [D01, D07].

Risks include potential compression of margins by powerful streaming platforms and the inherent difficulty in forecasting standalone free cash flow given the current reliance on content investment [D03, D05]. We must ensure that the transition to an independent company confirms our thesis on the sustainability of royalty cash flows [D05].

We have decided to PASS on this investment at this time. Despite the high quality of the underlying assets, the lack of standalone financial transparency and the hard-fail on current cash flow predictability lead us to exercise caution until further data becomes available post-listing.

valuation.eps_path: Mid-teens annual revenue and EBITA growth
valuation.downside_case: Margin compression from streaming platform power, mitigated by €30B transaction anchor

drivers.driver: Universal Music Group is the world's leading music entertainment company, possessing an unmatched, durable catalog and a dominant global market position [D01].
The business operates a high-margin, capital-light model that acts as a global royalty stream, directly benefiting from the secular growth of music streaming [D01, D03].
We have identified an attractive entry point at an enterprise value of €30 billion, consistent with recent private market transactions, offering an asymmetric risk-reward profile [D04].

The upcoming spin-off from Vivendi acts as a powerful catalyst, removing the conglomerate discount and technical overhang, allowing the market to re-rate UMG as a standalone pure-play leader [D01, D07].
Management, led by Lucian Grainge, has demonstrated a strong record of scaling the business and navigating the transition to digital, supported by robust governance [D01, D04].

kill_criteria: Structural reduction in royalty splits forced by streaming platforms
Shift toward high-capex content acquisition business models
Significant loss of market share or failure to retain core talent
Cancellation or disadvantageous restructuring of the spin-off
final.what_would_change_our_mind: A fundamental shift in the streaming royalty economic model that materially reduces margins, or a failure to maintain UMG's competitive moat against other majors and independent labels.
final.memo:
Universal Music Group is the dominant global leader in music, boasting an extensive, high-quality catalog and a capital-light business model that serves as a royalty-like engine for the digital age [D01]. By developing world-class talent and monetizing content across platforms, the company captures the compounding benefits of secular streaming adoption [D01, D03]. With 443 million paid subscribers globally at the end of 2020, UMG is uniquely positioned to benefit from the ongoing expansion of the music ecosystem [D01, D06].

Historically, the market has mispriced UMG by burying it within the Vivendi conglomerate, resulting in a persistent complexity discount [D01, D05]. The pending spin-off is the catalyst required to unlock this value, as it will eliminate the parent company overhang and alleviate technical selling pressure from passive holders unable to own the new security [D01, D07]. We are acquiring our stake at an enterprise value of approximately €30 billion, a valuation anchored by recent third-party investments that we believe significantly underestimates the company's long-term intrinsic value [D04].

Our investment thesis is built on an earnings path of mid-teens EBITA growth, driven by streaming revenue outstripping legacy declines and continued margin expansion [D01, D04]. At an entry multiple of 22.6x 2020 EV/EBITA, we view the valuation as attractive for a business of this quality, providing an expected annual return exceeding our 20% threshold [D04]. The risk of margin compression due to streaming platform bargaining power is the primary headwind, yet we believe UMG’s indispensability to these platforms provides sufficient protection [D05].

We are initiating a 10% position in Universal Music Group, reflecting our high conviction in the business’s durable growth and the clarity of the pending spin-off catalyst [D01]. We intend to hold this as a long-term core compounder in the Pershing Square portfolio, benefiting from its dominant, free-cash-flow-generative economics [D01, D04].
